library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Qin_2026_enoxacin"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.70314> (open access, PMC13428028)
* Models: `Qin_2026_enoxacin`, `Qin_2026_erlotinib`, `Qin_2026_gefitinib`,
  `Qin_2026_imatinib`

Qin and colleagues built GastroPlus 9.8.2 PBPK models (ACAT absorption plus
a compartmental disposition model) for 14 weakly basic drugs, used them to
simulate the loss of oral exposure when an acid-reducing agent (ARA) raises
gastric pH (Table 1), varied the drug properties one at a time to find the
eight that drive that loss, generated 4339 virtual drugs from them, and
trained an XGBoost model that predicts the ARA AUC ratio from 21 drug
properties (Table 2). The XGBoost model was checked against eight further
drugs (Table 3) and is offered as a web tool.

## What these models contain

Each of the 14 PBPK models has a systemic layer that is not a whole-body
PBPK model but a GastroPlus compartmental model: central volume and
clearance per kg body weight and first-order distribution rate constants,
printed in the row 'Disposition model parameters' of Supplementary Table
S1. For four drugs the authors fitted that layer to a published mean
**intravenous** profile, and Supplementary Table S3 compares the
simulated intravenous AUC and Cmax with the observed values:

| Model | Structure | Fitted to (Supplementary Table S1) | IV arms checked (Supplementary Tables S2, S3) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Qin_2026_enoxacin` | 3-compartment | Jaehde 1995, 428 mg over 1 h | 428 mg (Jaehde 1995); 200 and 800 mg (Chang 1988), all over 1 h |
| `Qin_2026_erlotinib` | 2-compartment | Frohna 2006, 25 mg over 0.5 h | 25 mg over 0.5 h (Frohna 2006) |
| `Qin_2026_gefitinib` | 3-compartment | Swaisland 2005, 50 and 100 mg over 1 h | 50 and 100 mg over 1 h (Swaisland 2005) |
| `Qin_2026_imatinib` | 3-compartment | Peng 2004, 100 mg over 1 h | 100 mg over 1 h (Peng 2004) |

These four intravenous disposition models are packaged here, with volume
and clearance proportional to body weight (`WT`, kg) as GastroPlus scales
per-kg compartmental parameters.

## What is not included

* **The XGBoost model.** It is a gradient-boosted tree ensemble with no
  equations or published trees; it cannot be written as an rxode2 model.
* **The oral ACAT layer and the ARA interaction.** The pH-dependent
  dissolution, precipitation and absorption along the GastroPlus ACAT gut
  are built into the platform; the paper prints only the drug inputs
  (solubility by pH, pKa, Peff, particle radius, precipitation time), not
  the gut physiology or the equations that use them. The ARA effect acts
  only through this layer, so Table 1 cannot be reproduced without it.
* **The other ten drugs.** Their disposition rows were either fitted to
  oral data through the ACAT model, so the clearance is calibrated against
  a bioavailability the paper does not print and no intravenous check
  exists, or they were carried over from other publications:

| Drug | Disposition source in Supplementary Table S1 | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Axitinib, ceritinib, dipyridamole, indinavir, lapatinib | 'Oral data-fitted estimation (calibrated via bioavailability)' | No intravenous check |
| Nilotinib | 'Oral data-fitted estimation (calibrated via bioavailability)' | Printed as 'Vc = 0.337 L/5kg', 'CL = 11.530 L/h/kg' |
| Entrectinib, dacomitinib, dasatinib | Parrott et al., Liu et al., Wang et al. | Earlier publications; dacomitinib CL printed as '045409 L/h/kg' |
| Propranolol | 'GastroPlus' | The intravenous check fails (see "Propranolol" below) |

# Population

No individual data were fitted. Each model was fitted to a published mean
profile in healthy volunteers (Supplementary Table S2):

* Enoxacin: Jaehde 1995, 12 subjects, mean age 27.9 years, mean weight
  76.1 kg. Chang 1988: 8 subjects, mean age 24 years, mean weight 69.5 kg.
* Erlotinib: Frohna 2006, 20 subjects, mean age 33.7 years; weight not
  reported.
* Gefitinib: Swaisland 2005, ages 18 to 65 years; number and weight not
  reported for the intravenous studies.
* Imatinib: Peng 2004, 17 subjects aged 40 to 58 years, mean weight
  73.3 kg.

# Source trace

| Quantity | Enoxacin | Erlotinib | Gefitinib | Imatinib | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lvc` (L/kg) | log(0.249) | log(0.695) | log(1.046) | log(0.247) | Suppl. Table S1 'Vc' |
| `lcl` (L/h/kg) | log(0.384) | log(0.059) | log(0.792) | log(0.189) | Suppl. Table S1 'CL' |
| `lk12` (1/h) | log(4.85) | log(0.215) | log(6.237) | log(4.471) | Suppl. Table S1 'k12' |
| `lk21` (1/h) | log(2.321) | log(0.141) | log(0.547) | log(1.226) | Suppl. Table S1 'k21' |
| `lk13` (1/h) | log(3.032) | -- | log(0.237) | log(1.706) | Suppl. Table S1 'k13' |
| `lk31` (1/h) | log(0.500) | -- | log(0.031) | log(0.219) | Suppl. Table S1 'k31' |
| Structure | 3-cmt | 2-cmt | 3-cmt | 3-cmt | Methods 'ACAT model and compartmental parameters'; number of rate constants in Suppl. Table S1 |
| Volume and CL per kg | yes | yes | yes | yes | Suppl. Table S1 units (L/kg, L/h/kg) |
| IV doses, infusion times, weights | see below | | | | Suppl. Table S2 |
| IV AUC and Cmax (observed, predicted) | see below | | | | Suppl. Table S3 |

The k31 printed for enoxacin is '0.500'. Supplementary Table S3 prints
the enoxacin AUC and Cmax in ug*h/mL and ug/mL although its header says
ng; they are converted to ng below.

# Simulation of the intravenous arms

Every intravenous arm of Supplementary Table S3 is simulated with the
infusion time and mean body weight of Supplementary Table S2. The
erlotinib and gefitinib studies do not report body weight; for them the
weight is set to the value at which the model's AUC (dose / CL) equals the
paper's predicted AUC, so for those three arms the AUC agrees by
construction and only Cmax is a check. Cmax / AUC does not depend on
weight, and it is checked separately below.

```{r arms}
arms <- data.frame(
  model = c(
    rep("Qin_2026_enoxacin", 3), "Qin_2026_erlotinib",
    rep("Qin_2026_gefitinib", 2), "Qin_2026_imatinib"
  ),
  drug = c(rep("Enoxacin", 3), "Erlotinib", rep("Gefitinib", 2), "Imatinib"),
  treatment = c(
    "Enoxacin 428 mg (Jaehde 1995)", "Enoxacin 200 mg (Chang 1988)",
    "Enoxacin 800 mg (Chang 1988)", "Erlotinib 25 mg (Frohna 2006)",
    "Gefitinib 100 mg (Swaisland 2005)", "Gefitinib 50 mg (Swaisland 2005)",
    "Imatinib 100 mg (Peng 2004)"
  ),
  dose = c(428, 200, 800, 25, 100, 50, 100),
  dur = c(1, 1, 1, 0.5, 1, 1, 1),
  wt_reported = c(76.1, 69.5, 69.5, NA, NA, NA, 73.3),
  # Supplementary Table S3, ng*h/mL and ng/mL (enoxacin converted from ug).
  auc_pred = c(14.62, 7.482, 29.94, 5.6661, 1.6606, 0.91456, 7.203) * 1000,
  cmax_pred = c(4.06, 2.08, 8.31, 0.45929, 0.21374, 0.1188, 1.1313) * 1000,
  auc_obs = c(15.15, 6.627, 31.80, 6.1907, 1.7508, 1.1169, 7.3862) * 1000,
  cmax_obs = c(4.14, 1.81, 6.58, 0.49554, 0.23561, 0.1027, 1.1693) * 1000
)

cl_per_kg <- c(
  Qin_2026_enoxacin = 0.384, Qin_2026_erlotinib = 0.059,
  Qin_2026_gefitinib = 0.792, Qin_2026_imatinib = 0.189
)
arms <- arms |>
  mutate(
    wt_implied = dose / (auc_pred / 1000) / unname(cl_per_kg[model]),
    WT = ifelse(is.na(wt_reported), wt_implied, wt_reported)
  )

arms |>
  select(treatment, dose, dur, wt_reported, wt_implied) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "IV arm" = treatment, "Dose (mg)" = dose, "Infusion (h)" = dur,
    "Reported weight (kg)" = wt_reported,
    "Weight implied by predicted AUC (kg)" = wt_implied
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

Where the weight is reported, the weight implied by the paper's predicted
AUC matches it within 0.3%, which confirms that the paper simulated each
arm at the study's mean weight with the per-kg clearance of Table S1.

```{r simulate}
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 4, by = 0.01), seq(4.25, 48, by = 0.25), seq(49, 480, by = 1))))

simulate_arm <- function(arm) {
  events <- bind_rows(
    data.frame(time = 0, amt = arm$dose, rate = arm$dose / arm$dur, evid = 1),
    data.frame(time = obs_times, amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0)
  ) |>
    mutate(id = 1L, cmt = "central", WT = arm$WT) |>
    arrange(time, desc(evid))
  rxode2::rxSolve(readModelDb(arm$model), events = events, returnType = "data.frame") |>
    mutate(id = 1L, treatment = arm$treatment, drug = arm$drug, Cc_ng = 1000 * Cc)
}

sim <- bind_rows(lapply(split(arms, seq_len(nrow(arms))), simulate_arm))
```

```{r profiles, fig.cap = "Simulated plasma concentrations after each intravenous infusion of Supplementary Table S3, at the study weights above (compare Supplementary Figures S4, S6, S7 and S8 of Qin 2026)."}
ggplot(filter(sim, time <= 48, Cc_ng > 0), aes(time, Cc_ng, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~drug, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "Concentration (ng/mL)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 2))
```

# NCA against Supplementary Table S3

```{r nca}
conc <- sim |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc_ng)) |>
  select(treatment, id, time, Cc_ng)
dose_df <- arms |>
  transmute(treatment, id = 1L, time = 0, dose, dur)
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc_ng ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  dose_df, dose ~ time | treatment + id,
  route = "intravascular", duration = "dur"
)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
sim_nca <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "aucinf.obs")) |>
  select(treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)

ref_nca <- arms |>
  transmute(treatment, cmax = cmax_pred, aucinf.obs = auc_pred)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  sim_nca, ref_nca,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated NCA against the paper's predicted intravenous values (Supplementary Table S3).")
```

```{r nca-check}
chk <- sim_nca |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  inner_join(arms, by = "treatment") |>
  mutate(
    auc_diff = 100 * (aucinf.obs - auc_pred) / auc_pred,
    cmax_diff = 100 * (cmax - cmax_pred) / cmax_pred,
    ratio_diff = 100 * ((cmax / aucinf.obs) / (cmax_pred / auc_pred) - 1)
  )
chk |>
  select(treatment, auc_diff, cmax_diff, ratio_diff) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "IV arm" = treatment, "AUC0-inf % diff" = auc_diff,
    "Cmax % diff" = cmax_diff, "Cmax/AUC % diff" = ratio_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

stopifnot(
  # Deterministic typical-value solves: AUC0-inf of a linear model is
  # dose / CL, so a mis-transcribed clearance or weight moves it at once.
  all(abs(chk$auc_diff) < 2),
  # Cmax at the end of the infusion depends on Vc and the distribution
  # rate constants; the paper's simulated value is matched within 10%.
  all(abs(chk$cmax_diff) < 10),
  # The weight-free check.
  all(abs(chk$ratio_diff) < 10)
)
```

The AUC agrees within 1% for every arm, and Cmax within 2.6 to 7%: above
the paper's predicted value for enoxacin, gefitinib and imatinib and below
it for erlotinib. The paper does not say how its Cmax was read (for
example, on what output time grid). The Cmax/AUC ratio, which does not
depend on weight, agrees to the same degree, so the differences come from
the peak itself rather than from the weights used here.

## Against the observed values

For reference, the observed values that the paper compared its
predictions with (Supplementary Table S3) are tabulated here; the
differences are the model's own prediction errors, which the paper
reports as R values (predicted / observed) within 0.82 to 1.26.

```{r observed}
cmp_obs <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  sim_nca,
  arms |> transmute(treatment, cmax = cmax_obs, aucinf.obs = auc_obs),
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ng/mL", aucinf.obs = "ng*h/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 30
)
knitr::kable(cmp_obs, caption = "Simulated NCA against the observed intravenous values (Supplementary Table S3).")
```

# Propranolol

The propranolol disposition row of Supplementary Table S1 (Vc 2.19 L/kg,
CL 0.752 L/h/kg, k12 0.291 1/h, k21 0.641 1/h, source 'GastroPlus') was not
packaged because it does not reproduce the paper's own intravenous
prediction. Solving it with the two-compartment erlotinib model's
structure for the 2.2 mg infusion over 0.25 h of Cid 1986:

```{r propranolol}
prop_par <- c(
  lvc = log(2.19), lcl = log(0.752), lk12 = log(0.291), lk21 = log(0.641)
)
prop_events <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(time = 0, amt = 2.2, rate = 2.2 / 0.25, evid = 1),
  data.frame(time = c(seq(0, 1, by = 0.005), seq(1.25, 72, by = 0.25)), amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0)
) |>
  mutate(cmt = "central") |>
  arrange(time, desc(evid))
prop <- bind_rows(lapply(c(60, 66), function(w) {
  rxode2::rxSolve(
    readModelDb("Qin_2026_erlotinib"),
    params = prop_par,
    events = mutate(prop_events, WT = w),
    returnType = "data.frame"
  ) |>
    summarise(
      weight = w,
      auc = 1000 * 2.2 / (0.752 * w),
      cmax = 1000 * max(Cc)
    )
}))
prop |>
  mutate(auc_pred = 48.74, cmax_pred = 12.23) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Weight (kg)" = weight, "AUC0-inf (ng*h/mL)" = auc,
    "Cmax (ng/mL)" = cmax, "Paper AUC" = auc_pred, "Paper Cmax" = cmax_pred
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

At the study's mean weight (66 kg) the AUC is 9% below and the Cmax 15%
above the paper's predicted values; the weight that matches the AUC
(60 kg) moves Cmax further away. No weight reproduces both, so the
printed row is not the one the paper simulated, and its source
('GastroPlus') names no study to check it against.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Only the intravenous disposition layer is packaged.** The oral ACAT
  model, the ARA interaction and the XGBoost model are not (see "What is
  not included"). Oral doses of these models would need an absorption
  model and a bioavailability that the paper does not print.
* **Ten of the fourteen drugs are not packaged**, for the reasons in the
  table above.
* **Weights for erlotinib and gefitinib** are not reported in
  Supplementary Table S2; the simulations here use the weight at which the
  model reproduces the paper's predicted AUC (74.8, 76.0 and 69.0 kg). The
  models themselves take any `WT`.
* **Parameter nature.** The parameters were fitted by the authors to one
  mean profile per drug, without between-subject or residual variability.
  The models are deterministic typical-value models.
* **Units.** Supplementary Table S3 reports the enoxacin AUC and Cmax in
  ug units under an ng header; the magnitudes (dose / CL at 76.1 kg =
  14.65 ug*h/mL against 14.62) confirm the ug reading.
* **Infusions.** The intravenous doses are constant-rate infusions over the
  durations of Supplementary Table S2.
